anyhow.whatItIs: A Rust library for passing application errors with context.
notGoodAt: Defining a public error contract; use typed errors.
anyhow.example: Add context when a file cannot be read.

serde.whatItIs: A Rust framework for converting data to and from typed values.
notGoodAt: Choosing a storage system; add one separately.
serde.example: Convert a saved record into a Rust struct.

serde_json.whatItIs: A Rust library for reading and writing JSON with Serde.
notGoodAt: Validating product rules by itself; add checks.
serde_json.example: Read a JSON settings document into a Rust value.

specta.whatItIs: A Rust library for exporting type definitions to other languages.
goodAt: Sharing Rust data shapes with frontend code
notGoodAt: Providing desktop commands; use a desktop framework.
specta.example: Export a Rust result type for a frontend.

specta-typescript.whatItIs: Exports Rust type definitions from Specta for use in TypeScript.

tauri.whatItIs: A framework for desktop applications with web interfaces and Rust code.
goodAt: Connecting a desktop window to Rust logic
notGoodAt: Building the web interface for you; add frontend code.
tauri.example: Open a desktop window that calls a Rust command.

tauri-build.whatItIs: Adds build-time steps needed by a Tauri desktop application.

tauri-specta.whatItIs: A bridge that exports typed Tauri commands through Specta.
goodAt: Keeping desktop command types aligned with frontend code
notGoodAt: Implementing command behavior; write Rust handlers.
tauri-specta.example: Generate frontend types for a Rust desktop command.

tempfile.whatItIs: A Rust library for creating and cleaning temporary files and directories.
goodAt: Using temporary storage during tests or processing
notGoodAt: Keeping files permanently; choose a durable path.
tempfile.example: Write a temporary test file that is removed afterward.

thiserror.whatItIs: A Rust helper for defining structured error types.
notGoodAt: Handling errors for the caller; add that logic.
thiserror.example: Define a distinct error for an invalid input file.

tokio.whatItIs: A Rust runtime for asynchronous tasks and input/output.
goodAt: Running concurrent network and file tasks
notGoodAt: Providing an application framework; choose one separately.
tokio.example: Run an asynchronous network request in a Rust program.

tracing.whatItIs: A Rust library for recording events and grouping them with the work that produced them.
notGoodAt: Collecting logs by itself; add a subscriber.
tracing.example: Record an event while processing a desktop command.

tracing-subscriber.whatItIs: A Rust library for collecting and formatting tracing events.
goodAt: Sending Rust tracing events to output
notGoodAt: Creating application events; instrument the code.
tracing-subscriber.example: Print structured events from a Rust program.
